text:
Marta: Quick follow-up from the RFC — I'm proposing we separate 'demote' (make prefix no-longer-hot) from 'handback' (give ownership back to the sequencer) into two small state machines. avoids the current combinatorial races we keep debugging.

Sam: curious — can you sketch the invariant we're trying to preserve?

Marta: main invariant: at most one active owner for a prefix and any reader must see a monotonic residency generation for correctness. current single-state approach mixes intentions (evict vs transfer) and we get mismatched gens during concurrent demote+handback.

Rajeev: so two state machines = demote-sm and handback-sm? how do they coordinate without adding new races?

Marta: keep them orthogonal. demote-sm lives on cache node and controls local residency (HOT -> DEMOTING -> COLD). handback-sm is a network protocol with sequencer to transfer ownership. they share only a small stable token: residency_gen (int) and a tombstone epoch (string). coordination rule: handback can only succeed if its observed residency_gen == current residency_gen on the owner. otherwise it aborts and retries.

Anya: that sounds like generation-checking we already have but maybe simpler to reason about. what's the failure mode?

Marta: failure 1: staleness — a handback with older gen may overwrite a newer demote if we used naive bool flags. now it will fail fast and the sequencer will re-request. failure 2: double-demote racing with prefetch where prefill thinks it's hot. solution: demote emits tombstone epoch so prefill can discard stale responses.

Sam: can you show pseudo transitions?

Marta: sure:

```
# demote-sm (local)
HOT --on(evict_request)--> DEMOTING { residency_gen++ }
DEMOTING --on(demote_persisted)--> COLD

# handback-sm (networked)
START --on(handback_request(gen,epoch))--> if gen == residency_gen && epoch == tombstone_epoch then HANDBACK_COMMIT else HANDBACK_REJECT
```

Rajeev: where do we persist residency_gen? do we need a durable store?

Marta: not necessarily durable like DB. persist to the node's local durable metadata (the same place we persist shard snapshot). we need it to survive process restarts so race detection on join works.

Anya: metrics/alerts? How will oncall detect regressions vs current?

Marta: add three guards: (1) handback_reject_rate by prefix (>0.5% over 5m) -> paging rule; (2) demote_retries by node; (3) stale_prefill_hits where prefills are dropped due to epoch mismatch. infra-bot can emit events for (1).

infra-bot: canary deployment scheduled: service/kv-cache will roll canary tag "demote-split-v1" to 5% at 2025-11-03T18:00Z.

Sam: tests? this needs targeted concurrency tests. I suggest two new fuzz scenarios:
- concurrent(evict + handback) on same prefix
- prefill wins vs demote (simulate slow prefill reply)

Marta: agreed. test harness will simulate message reordering and node restarts. also add unit that asserts monotonic residency_gen per prefix across transitions.

Rajeev: rollback story? if canary shows increased tail latency?

Marta: quick rollback by disabling handback-sm optimistic path via feature flag (fall back to current handshake). demote-sm is strictly local so safe. can add telemetry gated on flag.

Anya: nyc: do we need to change sequencer APIs? looks like sequencer needs to accept a gen+epoch check with a typed error enum.

Marta: small API change: sequencer RPC: HandbackRequest { prefix, owner_node, observed_gen, tombstone_epoch } -> HandbackResponse { status: OK | REJECT_GEN_MISMATCH | REJECT_EPOCH_MISMATCH }. no other payload changes.

Sam: lgtm. please put a short design doc and a minimal state diagram in the RFC follow-up. I'm happy to help with tests. :thumbsup:

Marta: thanks — I'll draft the doc and open a PR with the canary patch + tests. planning to have the RFC follow-up PR by EOW.

Rajeev: tiny nit — include backwards compatibility note for nodes that haven't updated (they should reject with REJECT_GEN_MISMATCH and sequencer will queue a re-request).

Marta: good call, adding that.

Anya: thanks, this addresses a lot of the long-running traps we've seen.

Sam: ping me when PR is up and I'll run the concurrency fuzz locally.
